gates.title: Per-image licensing, archive capture, and public availability
gates.decision: No clearance authorized. Scouting recorded item-specific terms and in-page motion review; nothing acquired; release blocked.
gates.plan_assumption_checked: ASSET_PLAN.md:122 suggests 'YouTube clips (screenshot-able)'. That is not a rights basis: the standard YouTube license is not reuse permission, so YouTube leads are rights-blocked.
gates.shot_claim_checked: SCRIPT.md:805 'A Pentium-era PC booting up'. No free candidate shows a boot on a period PC, and no free candidate identifies a Pentium CPU. Only the H02 LGR lead carries a creator-stated Pentium (100MHz), and that is unverified on screen.

candidates.status: terms recorded; not acquired; boot not shown; CPU unverified

review_questions: No free clip shows a period boot: use the Pexels period set shot (optionally with the POST-code insert) with narration carrying 'booting', pursue H02 permission, or commission a separately approved labeled stand-in?
Windows 95/3.x splash screens are Microsoft-copyrighted UI and BIOS vendor logos are third-party marks: is incidental on-screen OS/BIOS UI acceptable if H02 or a stand-in is pursued?
Is the Free Art License attribution and Article 4 larger-work condition acceptable for the final video if the Commons clip is used?
Is a ~2.6x upscale of the 640x416 Commons clip visually acceptable as a brief insert?
Neither free candidate identifies a CPU: confirm the edit will not caption or imply 'Pentium' over them.
